evidence.claim: After the invasion, Roskomnadzor ordered media to rely only on official Russian sources, threatened sanctions for 'false information', and the authorities crushed anti-war protests.
evidence.title: Russian Federation: Authorities impose censorship on media and crush peaceful anti-war protests following invasion of Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: After the invasion, Roskomnadzor ordered media to rely only on official Russian sources, threatened sanctions for 'false information', and the authorities crushed anti-war protests.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights-monitoring statement with direct description of censorship rules and protest repression.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin's government through state media and policing organs
contrary_evidence: Russia said it was countering disinformation during wartime.
The measures still sharply restricted peaceful dissent and information access.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said more than 13,800 people had been arbitrarily arrested at anti-war rallies since February 24, and that independent media were being blocked or forced out.
evidence.title: Russia: Kremlin’s ruthless crackdown stifles independent journalism and anti-war movement
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said more than 13,800 people had been arbitrarily arrested at anti-war rallies since February 24, and that independent media were being blocked or forced out.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights-monitoring summary with concrete arrest counts and media-blocking claims.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to federal authorities under Putin through police, regulators, and courts
contrary_evidence: The authorities claimed law and order and wartime security.
The scale of arrests indicates repression rather than narrow public-order policing.

evidence.claim: Russia's Supreme Court upheld the shutdown of Memorial's rights arm, and supporters were barred from the courtroom while defense witnesses were refused.
evidence.title: Russia's Top Court Upholds Decision To Shut Down Memorial Rights Group
evidence.excerpt: Russia's Supreme Court upheld the shutdown of Memorial's rights arm, and supporters were barred from the courtroom while defense witnesses were refused.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report from a reputable outlet on a court decision affecting a leading civil-society group.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-institution action under Putin's political control, though the court formally issued the ruling
contrary_evidence: The state can argue this was an organizational-law matter.
In context, it functioned as civil-society suppression.

evidence.claim: Russia's Justice Ministry canceled the registration of Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International, and 13 other foreign NGO offices.
evidence.title: Russia: Government Shuts Down Human Rights Watch Office
evidence.excerpt: Russia's Justice Ministry canceled the registration of Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International, and 13 other foreign NGO offices.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct rights-organization reporting on an official ministry action affecting independent monitoring.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Putin's government through the Justice Ministry
contrary_evidence: The ministry could describe this as regulatory enforcement.
The effect was to weaken independent oversight and complaint channels.

evidence.claim: Russia's parliament ended the European Court of Human Rights' jurisdiction, removing a major external legal avenue for complaints and remedies.
evidence.title: Russian parliament votes to break with European Court of Human Rights
evidence.excerpt: Russia's parliament ended the European Court of Human Rights' jurisdiction, removing a major external legal avenue for complaints and remedies.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report on a formal legal-remedy cutoff.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Putin's political system and legislative majority
contrary_evidence: The government could claim judicial sovereignty.
The practical effect was to remove a remedy route for victims.

evidence.claim: After Putin announced partial mobilization, protests against the war and draft were dispersed across Russia and OVD-Info counted more than a thousand detentions that day.
evidence.title: В России жестко разогнали акции против мобилизации
evidence.excerpt: After Putin announced partial mobilization, protests against the war and draft were dispersed across Russia and OVD-Info counted more than a thousand detentions that day.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and city-by-city protest summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent Russian-language reporting with contemporaneous detentions data from OVD-Info.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Putin's mobilization decision and the police response under his government
contrary_evidence: Officials could call the rallies unauthorized.
The scale and speed of detentions show coercive suppression.

evidence.claim: Some people detained at anti-mobilization protests in Moscow were reportedly given military-registration summonses at police stations.
evidence.title: Detained protesters in Moscow given military registration summonses
evidence.excerpt: Some people detained at anti-mobilization protests in Moscow were reportedly given military-registration summonses at police stations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report based on OVD-Info and local testimony, with a concrete coercive practice documented.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the security apparatus under Putin because the practice followed his mobilization order and police custody
contrary_evidence: The authorities could deny the practice or call it administrative processing.
The reported linkage to detention makes it look retaliatory.

evidence.claim: OVD-Info said more than 730 people were detained across Russia during protests against mobilization.
evidence.title: More than 730 detained in anti-mobilisation protests across Russia - rights group
evidence.excerpt: OVD-Info said more than 730 people were detained across Russia during protests against mobilization.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report relaying rights-group detention counts from multiple cities.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Putin's mobilization decision and the state response
contrary_evidence: The state described the protests as illegal.
The reported detentions still indicate broad suppression.

evidence.claim: OVD-Info reported more than 21,000 arrests, at least 370 criminal defendants for anti-war statements, over 200,000 blocked internet resources, and 11 treason sentences in 2022.
evidence.title: Repressions in Russia in 2022
evidence.excerpt: OVD-Info reported more than 21,000 arrests, at least 370 criminal defendants for anti-war statements, over 200,000 blocked internet resources, and 11 treason sentences in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialized independent monitoring group with detailed annual statistics on arrests, prosecutions, and blocking.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Putin's government because the data reflect federal policing, prosecutorial, and regulatory choices
contrary_evidence: Russia could argue the cases involved extremism or wartime security.
The aggregate pattern is still one of sustained repression.

evidence.claim: Putin signed a law greatly expanding restrictions on what Russia labels 'LGBT propaganda', effectively suppressing public expression and further targeting a vulnerable minority group.
evidence.title: Putin signs law expanding Russia's rules against 'LGBT propaganda'
evidence.excerpt: Putin signed a law greatly expanding restrictions on what Russia labels 'LGBT propaganda', effectively suppressing public expression and further targeting a vulnerable minority group.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on a signed federal law and its direct effect on public expression.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 legal crackdown on vulnerable groups
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct personal attribution to Putin because he signed the law
contrary_evidence: Officials framed the law as defending traditional values.
The practical effect was broader suppression of LGBT people and expression.

evidence.claim: The report described pervasive torture by law enforcement, political prisoners and detainees, severe suppression of free expression and assembly, and crimes targeting LGBTQI+ persons and minorities.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Russia
evidence.excerpt: The report described pervasive torture by law enforcement, political prisoners and detainees, severe suppression of free expression and assembly, and crimes targeting LGBTQI+ persons and minorities.
evidence.source_locator: opening country-summary sections and prison/detention discussion
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official annual human-rights report summarizing multiple issue areas from the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level attribution under Putin's presidency, though many abuses are carried out by subordinate organs and local officials
contrary_evidence: The government can point to formal laws and occasional investigations.
The report still describes a broadly repressive environment.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on command-and-control discipline, custody, accident-prevention, and other nuclear safety procedures in 2022 is thin.
Direct evidence on expert governance and risk institutions is weak relative to the rhetoric and escalation evidence.
The package needs better household and distribution evidence, not just macro stabilization and state-budget outcomes.
Direct evidence that appointments and institutions translated into durable productivity investment is still thin.
Direct 2022 delivery evidence for health, education, housing, and food security inside Russia remains thin.
Implementation and take-up by region and group are not well documented.
Direct documentary proof of Putin's personal beneficial ownership, asset control, or hidden conflicts remains limited.
The appointment and accountability map is still too thin for a fully rounded honesty judgment.
Direct 2022 implementation metrics for procurement, output, and battlefield effectiveness remain thin.
The package still needs a cleaner separation between frantic adaptation, temporary stabilization, and genuinely effective goal advancement.
